summary: Ray, a technician, has finished repairing and maintaining a robotic rat on a worktable while a diagnostic server exchanges data with it over a co-ax line. After the rat rolls to its feet, a booming voice calls Ray's name, and he reluctantly prepares to turn around. The excerpt introduces Ziggy, a large balding black man with a fu-manchu moustache, a former hardware hacker now in administrative oversight, whom only Ray calls Ziggy.
one_line: Ray finishes repairing a robotic rat and is summoned by Ziggy, a retired hardware hacker turned administrator, in this fiction excerpt.
key_facts: Ray has replaced a bad electrical relay that caused the crampon problem before attaching new limbs to the robotic rat.
A co-ax fiber line runs from the rat's anus to the diagnostic server array, with the other end plugged into an access port in the rat's back.
Ray has examined the rat's carapace for structural integrity flaws and performed manual diagnostics on the three dozen or so servo-motors that serve as its joints.
Ray removed the motherboard access panel in the rat's flank and touched an electrode stylus to contact nodes while scanning a single line LCD display.
Ray hopes to avoid seeing this rat again for a hundred thousand kilometers or so after his standard maintenance.
The severed limbs were placed in a bin of damaged parts kept for scavenging, experimentation, or jerry-rigging replacements.
Ray considers turning around a bad idea as a matter of personal policy, though not turning around would be worse when Ziggy calls.
Ziggy is described as a large black man, balding, with a devastating fu-manchu moustache.
Ziggy is a hardware hacker retired to administrative oversight.
Ray is the only one who calls him Ziggy; everyone else refers to him as Section chief-level title cut off in the note.
Blowing off Ziggy would constitute a career-ending bad idea, according to Ray.
